newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia awards licence for power sale to Thailand.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia awards licence for power sale to Thailand.

text.p: The Malaysian government on Thursday awarded a licence to a private power producer to sell electricity to Thailand from its planned 300 megawatt (MW) plant.

Energy, Telecommunications and Posts Minister Leo Moggie who awarded the licence to Teknologi Tenaga Perlis (Overseas) Consortium Sdn Bhd, said the company will generate and sell the power to Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand.
The combined cycle plant will be built in northern Perlis state bordering southern Thailand and will be fuelled by gas. No project cost was available, said company officials.

Three of four shareholders in TTP Overseas -- YTL Corp Bhd, Alpha Intercontinental Sdn Bhd and Gerbang Sutera Sdn Bhd -- each hold a 30 percent stake. The fourth, Yayasan Islam Perlis, has a 10 percent stake.

Moggie also awarded a licence to Teknologi Tenaga Perlis Consortium Sdn Bhd (TTPC) to build a 650 MW combined cycle plant. Electricity generated by the second plant will be sold to state power firm Tenaga Nasional Bhd.
TTPC officials said the plant will cost 1.2 billion ringgit to build and will start operating in 2000.
Moggie said the government had in 1995 awarded one licence to TTPC to build the 650 MW plant, of which 300 MW of electricity generated was to be sold to Thailand.
But it decided in September last year to issue two separate licences to smoothen the management of power generation, the minister said.
TTPC shareholders consist of Alpha Intercontinental with a 30 percent stake, Landmarks Holdings Bhd (20 percent), Gerbang Sutera (20 percent), Tenaga (20 percent) and Yayasan Islam (10 percent).
